figures_added.what: Real-life line graph of taxi cost against miles: axis titles Miles and Cost (£), the fare line drawn from the £3 start rising at £2 per mile (gradient 2 in data units, verified). Only the given £3 intercept is labelled; the 4-mile cost (box 1 = £11) is deliberately not plotted so the common-sense calculation is preserved.

Coordinate grid showing A(1, 2) and B(5, 10) with segment AB and its midpoint M marked. Point coordinates match the problem text; M is drawn at the true midpoint (3, 6) but its coordinates are left unlabelled because finding them is the first guided step. The gradient -1 line and c=9 are not drawn, so the answer is not revealed.

Grid with two parallel lines: P = y = -3x + 2 drawn solid with its y-intercept 2 marked (given in the equation), and Q parallel to P through (1, 5) drawn dashed. Q is clipped to the region where its intercept (0, 8) falls off-grid, so the answer (c = 8) is not shown while the parallel relationship and the given point are both visible. Line endpoints computed from the actual equations.

notes: Diagram pass only: added inline SVG at the START of three displays; no question text, solutions, guided_steps, hints, or misconceptions were changed. All SVGs are theme-safe (currentColor axes/labels, soft #60a5fa/#f59e0b accents, no hard-coded dark text fills, no external refs) and self-contained (<3KB each). Coverage judgement: the remaining bank problems give their coordinates in the text or read m/c straight off an equation. Per the diagram spec, coordinate-given two-point problems and pure read-off problems are fine without a figure, and none are phrased 'the graph shows...', so forcing grids on them would both be the decoration the spec warns against and spoil the taught substitution method (the y-intercept would be readable). Figures were therefore limited to the three cases where a figure adds genuine exam realism without revealing the answer: the real-life opener graph, the midpoint scene, and the parallel-lines scene. Validator PASS; PATCHed live (204) and read back with all three SVGs present and solutions [9] and [8] unchanged.
